interest: This document is of significant interest to historians studying the prelude to World War II in the Pacific, as it illustrates how early (1931-1932) American and Dutch authorities were tracking Japanese penetration into Southeast Asia. It highlights Dutch colonial anxieties that Japanese commercial ventures—specifically petroleum concessions along the eastern coast of Dutch Borneo—might serve as a pretext or foothold for establishing naval bases and conducting espionage in the Indonesian archipelago. Additionally, the cross-reference to consular reporting from Singapore emphasizes the coordinated surveillance of Japanese maritime movements off North Borneo by Western powers a decade before Japan's 1941-1942 invasion.
overview: This file consists of a U.S. Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing records under decimal file 894.20256G concerning Japanese military activities, espionage, and reconnaissance in Borneo during the early 1930s. The document indexes two primary items: a September 30, 1931 report forwarded from Batavia by Consul Kenneth S. Patton to the Far Eastern (FE) and Western European (WE) divisions regarding Japanese oil concessions on the eastern coast of Dutch Borneo and Dutch anxieties over potential Japanese naval base establishment, and a July 15, 1932 cross-reference note to Singapore despatch No. 314 from Consul Lester Maynard detailing Japanese activities off the coast of North Borneo.

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet listing records from 1931 to 1932 regarding Japanese oil concessions, naval base concerns, and maritime activities in Dutch and North Borneo.
subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, summarizing communications filed under classification 894.20256G on Japanese military and espionage activities in Borneo. The first entry records a September 30, 1931 dispatch from Batavia by Consul Patton to divisions FE and WE regarding Japanese oil concessions along the east coast of Dutch Borneo, noting Dutch fears of naval base development and enclosing a map. The second entry notes a July 15, 1932 communication (Despatch No. 314) from Consul Maynard in Singapore concerning Japanese activities off the coast of North Borneo, cross-referenced to file 123 451/350.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Military Activities of Japan in Borneo
